OPPOSITION OF DEFENDANTS KATIE HALL, ESQ.
& THE NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN
TO PLAINTIFF’S MOTION FOR REFERRAL TO AN EARLY SETTLEMENT CONFERENCE
Defendants Katie Hall, Esq. and The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children [collectively, “NCMEC”], by and through undersigned counsel and pursuant to the Rules and Orders of this Honorable Court, hereby respectfully submit the following Opposition to Plaintiff’s Motion for Referral to an Early Settlement Conference [Doc. 133]. NCMEC respectfully requests that the Motion be denied, on the grounds that a settlement conference is highly unlikely to be productive, or a justifiable expenditure of the resources of this Court or the Parties. In further support, NCMEC states as follows:
Plaintiff contends that “given the number and scope of the pending proceedings, an early settlement conference may permit the parties to explore resolution before further judicial resources are committed.” Doc. 133 at p. 1. Plaintiff does not set forth any other reason as to why a settlement conference is appropriate at this juncture, in either his Motion or his Memorandum in Support [Doc. 134].

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document 136 Filed 11/09/26 Page 2 of 3 PageID# 1660
Of course, under Rule 16(a), this Court has the ability to order that the parties appear for one or more pretrial conferences, including for purposes of facilitating settlement. Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(a)(5). However, NCMEC respectfully submits that a settlement conference at this time would be premature and counter-productive. Unfortunately, the proverbial “ship has sailed” in terms of preserving resources; Plaintiff has sued NCMEC twice, attempted to amend a complaint and then voluntarily dismissed the action, then promptly re-filed a new lawsuit, amended the pleading in this matter, attempted to amend the complaint, then refused to comply with the Court’s order to file a redline, and now seeks to do so again so as to add NCMEC’s Chief Legal Officer as a named defendant, for no apparent reason other than to harass NCMEC and distract it from its Congressionally-mandated and admirable work. As such, Plaintiff’s claims of interest in conciliatory proceedings rings hollow, to say the least.
To date, Plaintiff has filed approximately 25 other motions in this matter (excluding motions to file sur-replies, declarations, etc.), needless objections to procedural orders, and is seeking in excess of $42,000,000.00 (Forty-Two Million Dollars), all because NCMEC responded to subpoenas—as instructed—without awaiting formal service of those subpoenas, as a courtesy to Plaintiff.
NCMEC has no interest in settlement, and respectfully submits that a settlement conference would simply waste more judicial resources, and cause NCMEC to incur additional fees and expenses, for claims that NCMEC contends are, at best, frivolous. While Plaintiff is correct that the pending proceedings are vast in terms of scope and number, Plaintiff alone has caused such voluminous proceedings. Flatly put, NCMEC believes that an early settlement conference would be a waste of both the parties’ and this Court’s time and resources, and respectfully requests that
